implicit-relations-s2.title: The curve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^3 + y^3 = 6xy</annotation></semantics></math>
implicit-relations-s2.html:
Implicit differentiation of x3+y3=6xyx^3 + y^3 = 6xy gives the formula in the table. The point (3,3)(3, 3) is on the curve.
A curve and its implicit derivative
Curvedydx\frac{dy}{dx}
x3+y3=6xyx^3 + y^3 = 6xy2y−x2y2−2x\frac{2y - x^2}{y^2 - 2x}

items.q: Differentiate the oval's equation implicitly and solve: find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math> in terms of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: A sign slip. From <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>y</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x - y - x\frac{dy}{dx} + 2y\frac{dy}{dx} = 0</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}(2y - x) = y - 2x</annotation></semantics></math>.

The product rule on <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">xy</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y + x\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math>; you kept only <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(4, 2)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-4, -2)</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Write an equation for the line tangent to the curve at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-2, 2)</annotation></semantics></math>. Enter the right side.

mistakes.why: The slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2 - 2(-2)}{2(2) - (-2)} = \frac{6}{6} = 1</annotation></semantics></math>, positive.

Use the point <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-2, 2)</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 2 + 1(x + 2) = x + 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: At the highest point <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 4)</annotation></semantics></math> of the oval, find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math>, which tells how the curve bends there.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = 0</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2, 4)</annotation></semantics></math>, but the second derivative is not. Differentiate the quotient, then substitute <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 4</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

Check the sign: the numerator is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0 - 2)(8 - 2) - 0 = -12</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find the slope of the curve at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3, 3)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Numerator <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2(3) - 3^2 = -3</annotation></semantics></math>, denominator <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3^2 - 2(3) = 3</annotation></semantics></math>: the slope is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The point <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 0)</annotation></semantics></math> is on the curve. What does the formula for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math> tell you there?
options: The tangent line is horizontal, because the numerator is 0
The tangent line is vertical, because the denominator is 0

The slope is 1, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>0</mn><mn>0</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{0}{0} = 1</annotation></semantics></math>

Nothing, because it gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>0</mn><mn>0</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{0}{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, which decides neither a horizontal nor a vertical tangent

items.q: Find the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>-coordinate of the point other than <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 0)</annotation></semantics></math> where the tangent line is horizontal. Give an exact answer.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^3 = 16</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mroot><mn>16</mn><mn>3</mn></mroot></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = \sqrt[3]{16}</annotation></semantics></math>; take the cube root.

Substitute <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = \frac{x^2}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> into the curve: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^3 + \frac{x^6}{8} = 3x^3</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^3 = 16</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + y^2 = 25</annotation></semantics></math>, find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}</annotation></semantics></math> at the point <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3, 4)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{3}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(3, 4)</annotation></semantics></math>. Differentiate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{x}{y}</annotation></semantics></math> again with the quotient rule.

Use <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{3}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> inside: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><mn>16</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -\frac{y - x\frac{dy}{dx}}{y^2} = -\frac{4 + \frac{9}{4}}{16}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The curve <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^y + xy = e</annotation></semantics></math> passes through <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0, 1)</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx}</annotation></semantics></math> there. Give an exact answer.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>y</mi><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>y</mi></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>e</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{y}{e^y + x} = -\frac{1}{e}</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>e</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e</annotation></semantics></math> is in the denominator.
